o1.biggest_strength: Leads with the quiz data, puts the right product in the first email, and answers the sunscreen objections without overclaiming; the start-slow guidance is practical and safe.
o1.biggest_mistake: It assumes no code expiry, so it misses the deadline reminder the owner hoped for; if the 10% code does expire, the series needs a deadline line.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Confirm the code expiry and add a calm deadline nudge in Email 5 or the WhatsApp message, add after-discount prices, and drop in final links, postal address and legal footer.

o2.biggest_strength: Good data summary, clear three-way product split, strong sunscreen objection email, and a useful marketplace-order note.
o2.biggest_mistake: It invents a 14-day code expiry and builds urgency on it, and Email 5 uses the 2% salicylic acid face wash morning and night, which is too aggressive for beginners.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make code expiry a stated assumption or remove it, fix the routine to once-daily acid at night and rinse-only mornings, and keep the deadline reminder only if approved.

reason: Output 1 is the safer, more precise series: it segments from the first email, keeps the routine beginner-safe, and avoids inventing urgency. Output 2 has good touches, but the fake 14-day code deadline and twice-daily salicylic acid routine are the kind of mistakes I would not want to send.
